frozen_original.title: They're Eating the Dogs: Springfield Ohio Haitian Pet-Eating Hoax Drives 2025 Immigration Crackdown
frozen_original.synopsis: The Haitians are eating pets disinformation campaign — launched from a fourth-hand Facebook post in a local Springfield, Ohio crime group — was amplified into national policy by Trump and JD Vance, with consequences that continued to shape immigration enforcement throughout 2025. Vance posted the baseless claim on September 9, 2024 to 11.1 million views on X, and Trump repeated it on the debate stage on September 11, 2024 — They're eating the dogs. They're eating the cats. They're eating the pets of the people that live there — despite debate moderators immediately citing Springfield's own city manager confirming no credible reports existed. Springfield Mayor Rob Rue and police repeatedly confirmed there were no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed, injured or abused by individuals within the immigrant community, and the one animal-cruelty case cited had occurred 160 miles away in Canton and involved a non-Haitian Ohio resident. The campaign continued to drive policy in 2025: the Trump administration cut Haitian Temporary Protected Status short by six months, setting expiration for August 3, 2025 rather than the original December deadline, stripping legal protection from thousands of Haitians who had arrived through lawful humanitarian parole programs. PolitiFact documented that Vance had cherry-picked limited statistics to claim an 81% murder spike linked to Springfield's Haitian community — a figure that masked a longer-term crime decline — and White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt continued to characterize all humanitarian parolees as illegal immigrants, despite federal judges ruling the characterization legally false.

primary.split_explanation: The supplied parent combines the September 2024 Springfield pet-eating rumor with Haiti’s separate TPS policy and court history. The sources support two distinct children. The claimed causal link from the rumor to the TPS decision is unsupported and is omitted.

children.title: Springfield Faces Threats and School Disruptions Amid False Pet-Eating Claims
children.description_short: Springfield Faces Threats and School Disruptions Amid False Pet-Eating Claims
children.description_medium: PBS NewsHour reported on September 17, 2024, that false claims about Haitian immigrants stealing and eating pets had been amplified by Donald Trump and JD Vance. Springfield officials told Reuters they had no credible reports supporting the claims. By the PBS report, the city had experienced threats, school closures, fear in the immigrant community, and a canceled festival; the report said no bombs or attacks had occurred.
children.description_long: PBS NewsHour’s September 17, 2024 report described Springfield after false claims about Haitian immigrants stealing or eating pets were amplified by Donald Trump and JD Vance. Reuters Fact Check reported the week earlier that the narrative surfaced online without credible evidence. Springfield police told Reuters there were no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed by members of the immigrant community. Reuters also documented that a Canton cat-killing case circulated online as support for the rumor involved a lifelong Canton resident who was not Haitian. By the NewsHour report, Springfield was dealing with multiple threats against city hall, schools, universities, and community centers. The reporter said no bombs had been found and no attacks had happened. City Manager Bryan Heck said pet-eating was not a problem, while bomb threats were. PBS reported that the city canceled its CultureFest partly because of the threats. This draft covers the rumor and the immediate Springfield response; it does not claim every threat came from the rumor or link it to a separate immigration policy.

children.title: Court Blocks DHS’s Planned September 2025 Haiti TPS Cutoff
children.description_short: Court Blocks DHS’s Planned September 2025 Haiti TPS Cutoff
children.description_medium: DHS’s July 1, 2025 Federal Register notice set a September 2 cutoff for Haiti’s TPS designation. A July 15 federal judgment stayed the earlier termination, making any cutoff no earlier than February 3, 2026; the September date did not take effect. USCIS later reported that a separate termination became effective July 27, 2026. This policy and court sequence is distinct from the Springfield rumor and from humanitarian parole.
children.description_long: On July 1, 2025, DHS published a notice that purported to terminate Haiti’s TPS designation at 11:59 p.m. local time on September 2. Reuters reported that the move concerned roughly half a million Haitian beneficiaries. On July 15, a federal court in Haitian Evangelical Clergy Association v. Trump entered judgment making any termination effective no earlier than February 3, 2026; Haitian beneficiaries retained TPS and work authorization through that date. The September 2025 cutoff therefore did not take effect. USCIS later reported that, following a separate 2026 decision, Haiti’s TPS designation terminated effective July 27, 2026. That later status does not mean the 2025 cutoff happened on time. This record documents the 2025 policy notice and its court-ordered delay, with later status supplied for clarity. No source supports a causal link between the Springfield rumor and the TPS decision. Temporary Protected Status is a statutory designation and should not be described as humanitarian parole.

frozen_original.title: Trump Drops All Jamal Khashoggi Accountability Measures at Start of Second Term
frozen_original.synopsis: Upon taking office for his second term in January 2025, Trump's administration immediately moved to eliminate all remaining accountability measures related to the 2018 murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi. This included rescinding the Biden administration's declassification and release of the CIA assessment naming Mohammed bin Salman as responsible for ordering the killing, withdrawing visa restrictions on Saudi officials involved in the murder, and ending a designated 'Khashoggi ban' on visa issuances. The actions were accompanied by a swift restoration of full diplomatic and economic engagement with MBS, who was welcomed as a key strategic partner. Khashoggi's fiancée Hatice Cengiz, who had sought justice for his murder for six years, condemned the actions as a complete betrayal and capitulation to authoritarian impunity.

primary.title: Trump Drops All Jamal Khashoggi Accountability Measures at Start of Second Term
blockers: No official notice, court filing, contemporaneous report, or other event-specific source located documents a January 21, 2025 repeal of the Khashoggi Ban or visa restrictions on people previously covered by it.

The 2021 CIA/Intelligence Community assessment was already publicly released; the supplied claim that its release was rescinded describes no identifiable action and is conceptually distinct from changing sanctions or visa policy.

The supplied record does not identify any affected visa-restricted individuals, rescission notice, or specific diplomatic/economic action that would support the claim that all accountability measures ended.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends All DEI Federal Contracting Requirements
frozen_original.synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order immediately ending all diversity, equity, and inclusion requirements in federal contracting. The order revoked decades-old affirmative action mandates that had required federal contractors to take steps to ensure their workforces were not discriminatory toward women and minorities. Contractors were required to certify in writing that they had eliminated all DEI programs as a condition of continued federal contracts. Billions of dollars in contracts with major corporations, universities, and nonprofits were conditioned on the abandonment of DEI initiatives. The order also directed the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to cease all civil rights enforcement related to DEI. Legal challenges argued the sweeping revocation exceeded executive authority and conflicted with existing civil rights statutes.

primary.title: Trump Revoked EO 11246 and Changed Federal Contractor DEI Rules
primary.description_short: A Jan. 21 order revoked EO 11246, set a 90-day transition, and limited contractor certification to DEI programs that violate federal law.
primary.description_medium: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump revoked Executive Order 11246, which governed equal-employment requirements for federal contractors. The order allowed contractors to continue under the January 20 regulatory scheme for 90 days during the transition. It directed agencies to require certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate federal anti-discrimination law; it did not require contractors to eliminate every DEI program.
primary.description_long: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump signed the order “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity.” Section 3 revoked Executive Order 11246, the federal contractor equal-employment order, and allowed contractors to continue complying with the regulatory scheme in effect on January 20 for 90 days. It directed the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to stop holding contractors responsible for affirmative action and related practices described in the order. The order also required agencies to add contract terms concerning compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws and certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate those laws. That language is narrower than the frozen entry's claim that all contractor DEI requirements ended immediately or that contractors had to eliminate all DEI programs. The order took effect as an executive directive on January 21, but the 90-day transition means the change was staged. This record describes the order and its text; it makes no claim about court outcomes or documented injuries to a specific contractor, employee, or protected group.
organization_tags: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs
